title: Bangladesh’s Youth-led NCP Struggles for an Independent Identity in Jamaat’s Shadow
author: Saqlain Rizve
text:
Leaders of the National Citizen Party at the launching ceremony of the party on Feb. 28, 2025, at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Credit: Saqlain Rizve
On September 19, National Citizen Party (NCP) convener Nahid Islam sharply criticized Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Rahman would eventually have to choose how to leave power, he said. “He must decide whether he will flee the country by helicopter or resign with dignity.”Nahid was not speaking at an NCP rally. He was addressing a long march organized by the Jamaat-e-Islami (JI)-led 11-party opposition alliance to press a seven-point demand, including implementation of the February referendum verdict, action on rising prices, the energy and fertilizer crisis, deteriorating law and order, and corruption. JI chief Shafiqur Rahman spoke at the same gathering.[...]
